newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia to give Khmer Rouge ultimatum on hostages.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia to give Khmer Rouge ultimatum on hostages.

text.p: Cambodian military officials on Thursday said they would tell infamous Khmer Rouge rebel leader Ta Mok to hand over 15 detained government staff or face attack.
"We will ask Ta Mok to get the officials and helicopter back very soon, during this week, or the Royal Cambodian Armed Forces will fight Anlong Veng," a senior military official said.

King Norodom Sihanouk said the government had been tricked when it sent the 15 officials via helicopter into Khmer Rouge-controlled Anlong Veng on February 14 to negotiate with the feared, one-legged Khmer Rouge chief of staff.
"There was no plan to sacrifice, also uselessly, a helicopter crew and officers to fall into the jaws of the Big Bad Wolf, the unacceptable Ta Mok," the king said in documents released by the palace.
He said the royalist FUNCINPEC party of his son Prince Norodom Ranariddh had been naive and irresponsible in sending the men.
Most of the missing are from co-Premier Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party. Ranariddh says the men are negotiating for the defection of Khmer Rouge hardliners, but co-Premier Hun Sen calls them hostages.
But officials from both FUNCINPEC and Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party decided to issue the military ultimatum, political and military sources said.
Ta Mok is based in Anlong Veng, where fewer than 2,000 Khmer Rouge hardliners are believed to be concentrated near the Thai border.
The Khmer Rouge, who led the brutal 1975-1979 "killing fields" regime that left more than one million Cambodians dead, have been decimated by defections since last August.
But hardliners in Anlong Veng have held out to fight the government that took power after U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993.
